Restrained
rē-strānd´
v. (held back, checked; rendering Hebrew kala, batsar, atsar, and kahah, Greek katapauo)
Latin restringere, to bind back. The word is used of rain, of wombs, of a whole rebellious race, and of two sons a father would not check.

Biblical Definition

God restrained the flood: “the rain from heaven was restrained” (Gen 8:2). He judged Babel because “now nothing will be restrained from them, which they have imagined to do” (Gen 11:6). Sarai said, “the LORD hath restrained me from bearing” (Gen 16:2). Moses had to stop the offerings for the tabernacle: “the people were restrained from bringing” (Exo 36:6). And of Eli: “I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not” (1Sa 3:13). Isaiah asks of God's mercies, “are they restrained?” (Isa 63:15). At Lystra Paul and Barnabas “scarce restrained” the people from sacrificing to them (Act 14:18).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines restrain as to hold back; to check; to hold from action; to repress; to hinder from motion or action.

expand to see more

RESTRAIN, v.t. To hold back; to check; to hold from action, proceeding or advancing, either by physical or moral force.

2. To repress; to keep in awe; as, to restrain offenders.

3. To limit; to confine.

4. To withhold; to forbear.

Key Scripture

1Sa 3:13 — "For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not."

Gen 11:6 — "And the LORD said, Behold, the people is one, and they have all one language; and this they begin to do: and now nothing will be restrained from them, which they have imagined to do."

Gen 8:2 — "The fountains also of the deep and the windows of heaven were stopped, and the rain from heaven was restrained;"

Gen 16:2 — "And Sarai said unto Abram, Behold now, the LORD hath restrained me from bearing: I pray thee, go in unto my maid; it may be that I may obtain children by her. And Abram hearkened to the voice of Sarai."

Exo 36:6 — "And Moses gave commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp, saying, Let neither man nor woman make any more work for the offering of the sanctuary. So the people were restrained from bringing."

Act 14:18 — "And with these sayings scarce restrained they the people, that they had not done sacrifice unto them."

Modern Corruption

Permissive fathers are praised for gentleness, and Eli's house was judged for ever because he restrained his sons not.

expand to see more

Eli was not a silent father. Second Samuel 2 records that he heard what his sons did and spoke to them — “Why do ye such things?… Nay, my sons; for it is no good report that I hear” — and the sentence on his house names the failure exactly: he restrained them not. He rebuked and did not remove; he spoke and did not act; the priests who lay with the women at the tabernacle door kept their office. The modern father who has “talked to” his children and calls it discipline should read 1 Samuel 3:13 slowly. God did not judge Eli for being harsh. He judged him for being a voice without a hand, and the judgment came on the sons, the father, the ark, and the nation in one afternoon.

Genesis 11:6 is the other face of the word: God restraining what man will not. A united humanity with one language had begun to build, and the LORD's judgment was that nothing would now be restrained from them — that unity in rebellion has no natural limit — so He confused the tongues. The scattering was a restraint, and it was mercy; the world has been kept from the worst of what it could do together by the same hand that stopped the rain in Genesis 8. What theology calls common grace, Genesis calls restraint, and it is the only reason the earth has been habitable since.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew kala (H3607), to shut up, withhold; batsar (H1219), to cut off, make inaccessible; atsar (H6113), to shut up, restrain; kahah (H3543), to rebuke, restrain; Greek katapauo (G2664), to cause to cease.

expand to see more

Hebrew kala (H3607) — to withhold, shut up; Genesis 8:2, Exodus 36:6, Psalm 40:9, 88:8.

Hebrew batsar (H1219) — to withhold, be inaccessible; Genesis 11:6, Job 42:2; atsar (H6113), Genesis 16:2, 20:18.

Hebrew kahah, piel (H3543) — to rebuke, restrain; 1 Samuel 3:13 only; Greek katapauo (G2664), Acts 14:18.

Usage

"“His sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not” — a voice without a hand."

"“Now nothing will be restrained from them” — why Babel was scattered."

"“The LORD hath restrained me from bearing” — Sarai's right theology and wrong plan."
